name: immersive_7_1_2
character: Discrete 7.1.2 immersive audio: the 7.1 ring plus a front overhead pair, the smallest true-height format. This project's copy allows the fold-down 7 dB per band, not 6, because the speaker decode of this cue measured 1-5 dB darker than its binaural stereo master from 1 kHz up (see `gate_note`).
label: 7.1.2 immersive (ITU-R BS.2051 System I)
sources: ITU-R BS.2051-3: System I is the 7.1.2 loudspeaker layout (System H plus a front overhead pair at +30 degrees)
ITU-R BS.1770-4: the LFE channel is excluded from the loudness measurement
The -3.0 dBTP ceiling is this project's delivery policy for a multichannel file that carries an LFE channel, not a measured acoustic value

Loudness is measured on the delivered channels with the layout's channel weights (ITU-R BS.1770, `loudness.method`: bs1770_layout); it used to be the loudness of the two-channel fold, which a project can still ask for with "stereo_fold"
The linked limiter (5 ms look-ahead, 120 ms release, at most 6 dB of reduction) and the fold-down band limit (6 dB) are starting values, not measured ones
gate_note: Measured on the certified render of Night Pursuit Cinematic: the two-channel fold of the 10-channel file against the stereo master, after level matching on 200-2000 Hz, is -0.6 dB at 500-1000 Hz, -2.2 dB at 2-3 kHz, -5.1 dB at 4-4.9 kHz and -4.2 to -4.4 dB above 5.6 kHz, a smooth tilt that did not move when the cymbals, the sirens, the strings or the brass were re-placed (-6.1 dB at 4426-4955 Hz in three renders). The stereo master carries the HRTF and ear-canal lift of the binaural path; a loudspeaker bed does not. The limit is 7 dB, one more than the shipped starting value (which the shipped file says is not measured); no other row of the target is changed.
